plan.title: Kill-switch plant guard (#6136) refuses a read-only existence check of the kill-switch file

narratives.Description: The always-on kill-switch plant guard treats a read-only existence check as a plant when the command also redirects stderr. This story narrows plant detection to a write destination in the same shell segment, allows a bounded print or console.log mention, and keeps real plants denied.
narratives.Overview:
1. Same-segment dest ownership for plant - plant only when the kill-switch basename is the quote-aware redirect operand, dest-flag operand, or dest positional of a write bin within the same shell segment (break at isShellConnectorToken); do not let unrelated redirect or hasWriteShape any-gt or any INDIRECT_WRITE_BINS token elsewhere promote a co-occurring read-path basename; stop killWriteBins forward scans at connectors — relieves: P1 — relieves: P3
2. Bounded print/console.log mention proof + full second-route reconcile - add a finite recognizer for literal-only Node console.log(...) / Python print(...) payloads with no extra statements, substitutions, evaluated args, or write expressions; that proof (together with ordinary proven-read/existence-probe segments) is the sole kill-switch mention allow across hasKillSwitchShellWriteInner, harvestInterpreterPayloadDests quoted literals, hasProtectedUnprovenReadOnlyDestOfWrite, redirectDestIsProtectedSettings, hasWriteShapedProtectedSettingsDest, inactiveShellTargetsProtectedStore, and harvestDestsOfWriteForRealpath; do not claim interpreterPayloadIsProvenReadOnly alone covers print; writeFileSync / open-w / ni / mixed print-plus-write stay denied; preserve authz/approved-scope; no general embedded-language parser — relieves: P2 — relieves: P1
3. Public hook/dispatcher fixture matrix - UAT inactive and active; assert ops []; real projectRoot; allow verbatim AGENTS.md #3039 compound (flag absent and present; deny != present); allow ls/test/Test-Path/Get-Item basename with stderr-redirect; allow redirect-before-read basename; allow touch ordinary then ls basename; allow quoted prose only-mention; allow node -e console.log(name) and python -c print(name); deny touch; echo redirect-to-basename; ln; curl -o; cp/mv onto; redirect dest IS basename; Write/Edit; ls ordinary then touch basename; node -e writeFileSync(basename); python open-w; mixed print-plus-write; omit unproven readers from allow row — relieves: P1 — relieves: P2 — relieves: P3

narratives.UserStory: As an agent following the temporary kill-switch check, I want a read-only existence check and a mention-only print to be allowed, so that the required check is not refused as a plant.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. In packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts, plant a kill-switch basename only when it is the quote-aware redirect operand, dest-flag operand, or dest positional of a write bin in the same shell segment, and stop the write-bin scan at a shell connector.
2. In the same source file, add a bounded literal-only Node console.log and Python print proof and use that proof, with ordinary read probes, as the only mention allow on the secondary protected-store routes.
3. Extend packages/core/src/authz/classify.test.ts and packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.test.ts so the public hook matrix allows the read-only check and denies touch, redirection onto the file, cp, and mv.
4. Add changelog.d/6188-kill-switch-readonly-existence.md as the release note.

audit-targets: pain-P1, pain-P2, pain-P3

Round-1 verdict: Prefer-A direction is sound, but the Bound remedy needs revision before implementation. Three material gaps remain.

1. pain-P1 / pain-P3: redirectDestSlice is not a destination parser. At the pin it returns everything after `>` up to a connector/newline, including later arguments; the caller then uses substring matching. Thus `ls 2>/dev/null .deft-directive-disable` still matches even after removing the final hasWriteShape promotion. Quoted report text such as `printf '%s' 'example > .deft-directive-disable'` also reaches the raw `>` scan. Require a quote-aware redirect operand bound to its command, not the current suffix slice. Cover redirects before/after read operands, append/noclobber, fd duplication, quoted prose, quote-split actual destinations, and both protected basenames. Do not globally change this shared helper without checking its other consumers.

2. pain-P2: narrowing hasKillSwitchShellWrite alone cannot deliver the proposed interpreter allow. The pinned harvestInterpreterPayloadDests explicitly harvests quoted literals even for reads/print (its #3764/#3728 comment states this). hasProtectedUnprovenReadOnlyDestOfWrite consumes that harvest, and classifyHookAuthzOps can emit protected_store through inactiveShellTargetsProtectedStore independently of the kill-switch predicate. A valid example is `node -e 'console.log(".deft-directive-disable")'`. The design must name and reconcile this second route, including the realpath harvest that reuses it, while preserving authz/approved-scope protections. Otherwise a local predicate fixture passes while the actual hook still refuses. Specify a bounded distinction between mention-only payloads and actual interpreter writes; an interpreter blanket exemption is not adequate. Pair the print fixture with `node -e 'require("fs").writeFileSync(".deft-directive-disable", "")'` and Python open-in-write-mode cases.

3. pain-P1 / pain-P2 / pain-P3: write-bin matching must bind executable, operands, and command segment. The current killWriteBins walk scans every token as a possible executable and then scans all remaining tokens without stopping at connectors. `touch /tmp/ordinary; ls .deft-directive-disable` therefore inherits an unrelated writer. Quoted issue/report prose containing writer names is another relevant case. Define destination ownership per command, including source-versus-destination for cp/mv/ln, rather than replacing the redirect heuristic while retaining this global co-occurrence rule. Add the paired deny `ls /tmp/ordinary; touch .deft-directive-disable` so a read prefix cannot suppress a real plant.

Required acceptance expansion: retain the draft's true-plant and Write/Edit denies, and exercise the allow/deny matrix through the public hook/dispatcher boundary, with UAT inactive and active, not just hasKillSwitchShellWrite. For pain-P3, test the actual AGENTS-style compound existence check with the flag absent and present: authorization must allow the read in either state; filesystem observation determines presence. A denial must not serve as presence evidence. No wording redesign is needed (#6139 stays out).

Evidence: static pin-read of packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts at e514bc81132ff8c3bfbb5f9cdf6490d80bfcdc5a; examples above are source-derived predictions, not executed tests. Read issue body and comments only through inclusive ceiling 6807770436. Critiqued draft 6807761767 against Stop 1 6807752729. No implementation or ingest performed.

Round-1 critic on Prefer-A draft 6807761767 against Stop 1 6807752729. Pin-read only at e514bc81132ff8c3bfbb5f9cdf6490d80bfcdc5a. Id ceiling inclusive 6807770436 (panel-deposit). No later thread reads.

## Pin evidence (hasKillSwitchShellWriteInner)

P1 path: after mentionsKill, redirectDestSlice already plants only when the dest region names a kill-switch basename (correct for echo >/basename). The over-match is the later exact-basename fallback: if a token is basename and hasWriteShape(command) is true, plant. hasWriteShape is command.includes(">") — so ls/test/stat/cat basename 2>/dev/null or >/tmp/out promotes the read-path token. Matches Stop 1 live matrix.

P2 path: killWriteBins spreads INDIRECT_WRITE_BINS (node/python/perl/ruby/pwsh/…). For those bins, any later pathishMentionsKillSwitch token returns true. pathishMentionsKillSwitch uses includes(basename), so node -e print(name) plants on the -e string. Matches Stop 1.

P3: AGENTS.md #3039 existence check is the P1 form; refuse-as-plant is the contract contradiction.

True plants on pin still hold: touch; redirect dest IS basename; ln/link/mklink; curl -o basename; Write/Edit via classifyHookAuthzOps writePath.

## Pain audit vs Prefer-A draft

| Pain | Draft limb | Relief on pin |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P1 | 1 redirect/write-shape | Yes — stop unrelated > from promoting read-path basename via hasWriteShape |
| P2 | 2 interpreter -e/-c/-p | Yes — mention-only interpreter string non-plant; require shell write dest/outfile/redirect to basename |
| P3 | 1 (via P1) | Yes — AGENTS.md ls/test/stat/cat + 2>/dev/null becomes admit once P1 closes |

## Findings

### 1. Prefer-A is the right lean (accept)

Two independent over-match limbs in one function; draft names both sites and keeps Stop 1 true-plant set. Spec-path correctly fences hasKillSwitchShellWrite / Inner. conflict_group kill-switch-plant-read-mention-overmatch fits. No Approach B/C needed for Stop 1.

### 2. Limb 2 must keep embedded-language FS write as non-goal (sharpening)

classify.ts header non-goal: arbitrary embedded-language semantics. After limb 2, node -e writeFileSync(kill-switch-basename) / python -c open(kill-switch-basename,"w") become ALLOW unless a shell redirect/outfile targets the basename. Stop 1 keep-list does not require denying those. Bound MUST state that interpreter-embedded FS plants stay non-goal (residual outside this classifier), so pain-audit does not thrash on false-open. Do not invent JS/Python write parsing in this Bound.

### 3. Fixture matrix must lock cp/mv onto basename (sharpening)

Stop 1 keep true plants includes cp/mv onto. Limb 3 deny list names touch; echo >; ln; curl -o; redirect dest IS basename; Write/Edit — omits cp/mv. killWriteBins already plants those today; fixtures must lock deny so limb 1/2 edits cannot regress them. Also lock allow for the AGENTS.md-shaped compound (ls/test/stat/cat basename + 2>/dev/null) and bare ls basename (already allow on pin).

### 4. Limb 2 implementation fence (sharpening)

Do not blanket-delete interpreters from killWriteBins / INDIRECT_WRITE_BINS (those sets feed other write-shape consumers). Gate only the kill-switch Inner any-arg pathishMentionsKillSwitch scan for interpreter -e/-c/-p string operands (or equivalent: interpreter + mention-only string is non-plant). Redirect dest IS basename remains plant for node … > basename. Scope edits to hasKillSwitchShellWriteInner (+ fixtures); do not change global hasWriteShape used by hasIndirectAuthzStoreWrite.

### 5. P3 is consequence-only (footnote)

Limb 1 claiming relieves: P3 is fine once P1 admit path is the AGENTS.md check. No separate AGENTS.md prose limb; keep docs as footnote per #5783 KISS.

## Verdict

verdict: accept-prefer-a-with-sharpenings
blocking: none
sharpenings: embedded-FS-non-goal; fixture-lock-cp-mv; limb2-gate-not-global-INDIRECT-delete; Inner-only-scope

Bind Prefer-A. Fold sharpenings 2-4 into Bound remedy list items (or explicit keep non-goal / fixture bullets under limb 3) before pain-audit. Reject widening into embedded-language plant detection or global hasWriteShape retune.

Producer 2 fires because `dests.push(...quotedStringLiterals(payload))` at :2617 is **unconditional** — the `interpreterPayloadIsProvenReadOnly` gate at :2622 guards only *unquoted* payload tokens — and `zipLiteralIsProtectedDest` (:2013) treats a bare kill-switch basename as a protected dest. That function's own docstring states the intent: "Reads and `print` of protected paths in those payloads classify unknown."

Today producer 2 is invisible, because the unknown arm is guarded by `!found.has("settings")` (:4710-4713). Bound 2 removes `settings` — which **satisfies that guard** and turns the unknown arm on. The call still refuses, under a different reason. And `hasProtectedDestOfWriteUnknown` (:5051), an exported public pin, has no settings guard at all: it returns true both before and after Bound 2.

Amend: Bound 2 must name the second site. Either gate the quoted-literal push at :2617 behind `interpreterPayloadIsProvenReadOnly`, or exempt kill-switch basenames from `isRelativePayloadProtectedDest` for proven-read-only payloads — as a Bound clause, not left to implementation. ## C2 — Bound 1 disarms one of hasWriteShape's two arms; the issue's own repro uses the other

`hasWriteShape` (:4315) has two arms: `command.includes(">")` (:4316), and *any* `INDIRECT_WRITE_BINS` token anywhere in the command (:4319). Bound 1 addresses only the first. The final promotion loop at :3687 ORs the whole function, so a `sed` / `node` / `cp` / `rm` anywhere on the line still promotes the read-path basename.

The `killWriteBins` loop above it (:3644 onward) is looser still: from any write bin it scans forward over all remaining tokens with no segment boundary, so `sed -n 1p AGENTS.md; ls .deft-directive-disable` denies on the forward scan, and the reverse order denies via :3687.

This matters because the repro in the issue body is compound: `cd <project> && ls -la <file> 2>/dev/null; <other read-only commands>`. The single-segment `ls <file> 2>/dev/null` in the pin evidence is a reduction of it. Relieving only the reduction leaves P1/P3 standing for the form AGENTS.md actually prescribes.

## Summary

The managed AGENTS.md (#3039) tells the agent to check for the root kill-switch file before loading Directive further. A read-only check of that file is refused by the #6136 plant guard, as if the agent were creating it.

Directive version: 0.129.6. Host: Claude Code.

Note on wording: this report writes the file name as `<kill-switch-file>` and paraphrases the refusal text. Bash calls whose text contains the literal file name, or the human-presence grant command that the refusal names, are refused by the hook, and that includes the call that files this issue. The first attempt to file it was refused by the authz-store guard, only because the body quoted the plant-guard message.

## Repro

The first Bash call of a session, following AGENTS.md "Temporary test kill-switch (#3039)":

```sh
cd <project> && ls -la <kill-switch-file> 2>/dev/null; <other read-only commands>
```

Result: the call is refused with the #6136 message "denied kill-switch / permanent opt-out plant without a human-origin settings grant". The message continues that agents must not self-serve the kill-switch or opt-out files, and that a human must plant them or grant settings.

`ls` only reads; nothing is created.

## Expected

The guard refuses commands that create, write or move the file (`touch`, redirection, `cp`/`mv` onto it, and so on). Read-only commands that name it (`ls`, `test -e`, `stat`, `cat`) are allowed, because AGENTS.md requires exactly that check. Text that only mentions the file or the grant command, such as in a heredoc body or a `--body` argument, is not treated as a write.

## Impact

AGENTS.md requires a check that the hook then refuses. The agent either skips the check or looks for a form the guard does not match. It can also wrongly report the refusal as a sign that the flag is present. Issue text and notes that mention these names cannot be written through Bash either.
